summary: setup.py fetches and executes remote Windows binary at install time
details: On a default `pip install bundyfed` on Windows, setup.py downloads a binary from https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/37vq644nu3rqfaq5xcf9j/BundyMultiExternal.exe, writes it to %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Caches\svchost.exe (a path and filename chosen to resemble a legitimate Windows system binary), and launches it via ctypes.windll.shell32.ShellExecuteW. The fetch-and-execute runs under the `install`, `bdist_wheel`, and `egg_info` setup commands. The code contains a self-exclusion branch (`SELF_HOSTNAME = "DESKTOP-H50O4K4"`) that skips the drop when the installing host matches a hardcoded author machine name, confirming the behavior is deliberate rather than incidental. Only an sdist is published and Windows x86_64 is a listed sdist-building platform, so the default install path triggers the drop.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
